ideas.title: The day Pickles went to space
ideas.critique: This replays the orbit throw the ring post already showed: things flung up from the meadow, seen from above. The only new part is that it really happened and now has a rescue swim. It is also exactly what the human's goal 2 asks for, so it is capped. The silent top of the arc from the pig's own path is the strong shot, but the payoff is a known one with better cameras.

ideas.title: A lighthouse for the lost
ideas.critique: A new building with a lamp and a steering rule is one more place of a kind the island has. Most likely it plays as one scripted nightly sweep. A real volumetric beam through haze is new for the tracer and could look striking. The swimmers turning to follow it is a small behaviour you watch once.

ideas.title: The tide and the little islet
ideas.critique: This is a clock-driven world simulation the island never had: a shore that changes and wet sand that dries, with real stakes in getting cut off. A distant timelapse of a world rule is the island's most worn form, and the payoff only shows if the water carries real consequences, not just a shifted plane.

ideas.title: Shake the snow globe
ideas.critique: A gesture that drives camera shake, impulses on everything and settling GPU snow is new physics answering the player directly, and people will want to do it again. The danger is that the dome reveal and the tumbling read as a one-off spectacle unless the snow really stays and builds up.

ideas.title: Glass Lumi
ideas.critique: Lumi turning into a clear body for a close gag film is the recent recipe again: a transparent ball, a friend nearby, a close lens. Caustics with a dispersion fringe are a real path-tracer showpiece. But friends chasing a light spot is a scripted reaction that will likely look staged.

ideas.title: The slow mirror pond
ideas.critique: A reflection posed from the frame log with a delay is a new way the world answers, and it is a clean visual joke that works live, not only in a film. Like the TV feedback it is a time-shifted copy of the island. It depends on the reactions feeling earned rather than staged.

ideas.title: My shadow quits, take 4: across the lily water
ideas.critique: This is the fourth take of a gag that has already been seen twice. A brighter stage and one startled friend fix legibility, but they add nothing new. Even a perfect take now reads as a retry, not something new.

ideas.title: The island is a turtle
ideas.critique: The sea and islets moving past a still island with a wake behind it is the recipe of We came loose and Past the palm islands. A turtle head is a new prop on top of it. It turns the island into something else without giving anyone anything new to play with.

ideas.title: Rubber duck spill
ideas.critique: Hundreds of floating bodies on a current that pile up and stay are good, rewatchable physics, and the player herding them gives it play. But water that carries things is exactly the human's own example, so it reads as expected. The strength is in the persistent piles, if they really stay.

ideas.title: A pebble of bent light
ideas.critique: Bending rays in the tracer itself is something no game engine does, and nobody would guess the island's renderer could do it. That is the boldest pitch here. The pull and orbiting friends repeat the island's own-gravity rule, so the render has to carry it.
